hyperedges.label: Three independent paths keep the graph fresh
Service classification gate: policy + checklist + CI enforcement
Two merge gotchas addressed by the service checklist
Async job lifecycle: submit (idempotency index) -> FIFO queue + keeper heartbeat -> worker -> hardened terminal write -> poll with stale-on-read
Five-layer saturation defense: route gate + isolated debug slots + inflight dedup + browser semaphore + server-side batch clamp
9-step detection flow: cache -> fetch (+variant gate) -> page validation -> challenge -> URL/HTML signals -> NLP -> alternatives -> decision matrix

The flood's causal chain: a 120 s belt around the fetch_html cascade inside check_page_if_french cancels mid-goto, leaving a pending-but-uncancelled protocol callback that Connection.cleanup() then poisons unreadably
The two-change fix: a single scrape_html probe stops the orphans being created, the narrow loop handler drains the residual, and the counter keeps what is silenced observable
The Playwright-pin dead end: the research, the falsified 'upgrading fixes it' claim, the Camoufox<1.61 ceiling, and the dismissed camofox-browser wrappers

The falsification set that bounded this fix: OOM-kill, Playwright process leak behind 876 PIDs, and CPU saturation all disproved by measurement, which withdrew the pids_limit recommendation and removed any case for a structural Playwright refactor
The three-change fix and the suites that guard it: variant denylist gate, liveness-aware teardown, exception drain
Detection asyncio unretrieved-exception flood lineage: inflight_dedup fut.exception() then this chantier's teardown drain (2026-08-03) then the orphaned goto-callback loop handler (2026-08-05)
Les 5 barrières qui rendent B2 inerte à la livraison (liste vide, flag false, aperçu par défaut, validation humaine, re-vérification sur lecture fraîche)
Les affirmations réfutées ou corrigées pendant l'investigation — reprendre l'une d'elles coûterait un cycle

Le principe transversal du chantier: aucune valeur n'est devinée — le stage vient du site d'appel, le stage 'browser' de l'absence d'écriture, et la liste de causes se remplit sur des libellés récoltés
One seven-condition predicate, three consumers: the pure module, the repair pass caller (which owns the lock probe), and the dry-run endpoint that must evaluate the same seven
The six conditions of the repair predicate, each closing a distinct way the evidence can lie
The deployment safety interlock: the allowlist file arms two disjoint consumers, only one of which the repair flag controls
What adversarial review changed: a fail-open freshness anchor, an overstated snapshot claim, a self-contradicting stat-error rule, and a deployment order that deleted before it measured
The rescue's effective budget is arbitrated by five constants at once (VARIANT_RESCUE_BUDGET_S, _ITEM_WALL_CLOCK_S, _RESCUE_MARGIN_S, _MIN_PROBE_S, JOB_MAX_S)
2026-08-11 async-job Redis resilience trio: submit 503, poll 503-vs-404, terminal-write deadline — and its operational cost
Rattrapage par variante d'URL : verdict inexploitable après fetch réussi → sondes bornées par budget → premier verdict français gagne
Observation lexicale au Cas 9 : compte de mots exclusifs distincts publié dans details, diagnostic écrit dans error, aucun verdict changé
Lignée des chantiers de faux négatifs FR sur la matrice de décision (Case 2a hreflang, strip consent, soft-French lexical, seam audit crawler/détection)
Contrat de fraicheur du marqueur .move-done: le daemon hote ecrit le marqueur, le predicat le date contre stashed_at, le garde le supprime s'il ne peut pas etre prouve notre

Famille « une preuve n'en est une que si elle est plus recente que ce qu'elle pretend attester »: garde .move-done et reparation du statut archived partagent la meme regle de datation et le meme fail-closed
The 2026-08-10 reclean freshness-guard chantier — spec, plan, task tracker, the shared predicate module, the destructive sweep and the two test suites that prove neutrality and the regression

The data-loss chain the guard closes: archive_crawl's two no-re-tar branches (one of them deleting its temp download) mark archived via _mark_as_archived, the allowlist loader attests the old tar, and the sweep deletes the newer local tree

nodes.label: WHY the retry must be explicit: redis-py defaults to Retry(NoBackoff(), 0) with an empty retry_on_error (verified 5.2.1), so the first command on a reaped socket raises ConnectionError and every cache_service helper swallows it into its default return (None/0/[]/False) — indistinguishable from a real answer; redis is unpinned so the default is whatever pip resolved
nodes.norm_label: why the retry must be explicit: redis-py defaults to retry(nobackoff(), 0) with an empty retry_on_error (verified 5.2.1), so the first command on a reaped socket raises connectionerror and every cache_service helper swallows it into its default return (none/0/[]/false) — indistinguishable from a real answer; redis is unpinned so the default is whatever pip resolved

nodes.label: WHY _with_retry (crawler_manager.py:61) does not cover reaped connections: cache_service helpers catch Exception internally, so the wrapper never sees a RedisConnectionError — the only error reaching it is the builtin ConnectionError('Redis is not connected.') raised when the client is None (an OSError subclass)

nodes.label: Terminal-write retry redone 2026-08-11: deadline-based backoff (0.5/1/2/4/8/8s) bounded by min(TERMINAL_WRITE_BUDGET_S, remaining JOB_MAX_S) read off time.monotonic(), replacing the fixed 3-attempt loop that exhausted in ~3.6s and could not survive a fast-fail Redis restart; a write lost when the budget runs out is counted under detect_async_jobs_terminal_total{status="lost"}, never completed/failed
nodes.norm_label: terminal-write retry redone 2026-08-11: deadline-based backoff (0.5/1/2/4/8/8s) bounded by min(terminal_write_budget_s, remaining job_max_s) read off time.monotonic(), replacing the fixed 3-attempt loop that exhausted in ~3.6s and could not survive a fast-fail redis restart; a write lost when the budget runs out is counted under detect_async_jobs_terminal_total{status="lost"}, never completed/failed

nodes.label: Why the terminal-write budget is clamped to the remaining JOB_MAX_S and read off time.monotonic(): _worker_loop's asyncio.wait(timeout=JOB_MAX_S) races the same clock, and a write still retrying when it fires gets cancelled by _abandon_job, which overwrites an already-COMPLETED batch with failed(job_timeout) — worse than the stale 'running' this retry exists to avoid
nodes.norm_label: why the terminal-write budget is clamped to the remaining job_max_s and read off time.monotonic(): _worker_loop's asyncio.wait(timeout=job_max_s) races the same clock, and a write still retrying when it fires gets cancelled by _abandon_job, which overwrites an already-completed batch with failed(job_timeout) — worse than the stale 'running' this retry exists to avoid

nodes.label: Known residual gap NOT closed (review 2026-08-11): the deadline only gates whether ANOTHER sleep-then-retry happens, it does not bound an attempt already in flight — the shared pool wraps every command in its own Retry(ExponentialBackoff(cap=1.0), 3) over socket_timeout=10s, so one hung socket can burn tens of seconds and a clamped budget can still return after JOB_MAX_S; deliberately not wrapped in wait_for, because cancelling mid-command would poison the pooled connection
nodes.norm_label: known residual gap not closed (review 2026-08-11): the deadline only gates whether another sleep-then-retry happens, it does not bound an attempt already in flight — the shared pool wraps every command in its own retry(exponentialbackoff(cap=1.0), 3) over socket_timeout=10s, so one hung socket can burn tens of seconds and a clamped budget can still return after job_max_s; deliberately not wrapped in wait_for, because cancelling mid-command would poison the pooled connection

nodes.label: Why TERMINAL_WRITE_BUDGET_S defaults to 60: REDIS_HEALTH_CHECK_INTERVAL_S (the shared pool's own setting) + REDIS_RECONNECT_INTERVAL_S (this service's lifespan reconnect loop in main.py, not a pool setting), 30s each — at least one full healing cycle of either mechanism, and half of STALE_THRESHOLD_S
nodes.norm_label: why terminal_write_budget_s defaults to 60: redis_health_check_interval_s (the shared pool's own setting) + redis_reconnect_interval_s (this service's lifespan reconnect loop in main.py, not a pool setting), 30s each — at least one full healing cycle of either mechanism, and half of stale_threshold_s

nodes.label: 503 differentiation corrected 2026-08-11: Redis-unavailable at submit (ping / claim_index / write failure) now sets Retry-After exactly like capacity does; the kill-switch _JobsDisabled (ASYNC_JOBS_ENABLED=false) is the ONLY 503 left without the header — an invariant callers key off and that must not be broken
nodes.norm_label: 503 differentiation corrected 2026-08-11: redis-unavailable at submit (ping / claim_index / write failure) now sets retry-after exactly like capacity does; the kill-switch _jobsdisabled (async_jobs_enabled=false) is the only 503 left without the header — an invariant callers key off and that must not be broken

nodes.label: Why a Redis-unavailable 503 must carry Retry-After: a caller that discriminates retryability by header presence would otherwise read a 2-second Redis restart as the permanent kill-switch and burn its whole retry budget on one chunk
nodes.norm_label: why a redis-unavailable 503 must carry retry-after: a caller that discriminates retryability by header presence would otherwise read a 2-second redis restart as the permanent kill-switch and burn its whole retry budget on one chunk

nodes.label: Poll 503 vs 404: JobStore.get() degrades both 'no such key' and 'Redis read failed' to the same None by design, so the poll handler tells them apart with a ping — ping fails gives 503+Retry-After (the BO sleeps and retries), ping succeeds gives 404, the only poll code that breaks the BO's retry loop
nodes.norm_label: poll 503 vs 404: jobstore.get() degrades both 'no such key' and 'redis read failed' to the same none by design, so the poll handler tells them apart with a ping — ping fails gives 503+retry-after (the bo sleeps and retries), ping succeeds gives 404, the only poll code that breaks the bo's retry loop

nodes.label: Known limit of the poll ping: it can borrow a different pool connection than the failed read, so a single poisoned connection can still produce read-fails-but-ping-succeeds and emit a spurious 404 that discards the whole in-flight chunk — the ping narrows this window, it does not close it
nodes.norm_label: known limit of the poll ping: it can borrow a different pool connection than the failed read, so a single poisoned connection can still produce read-fails-but-ping-succeeds and emit a spurious 404 that discards the whole in-flight chunk — the ping narrows this window, it does not close it

nodes.label: Operational consequences of the 2026-08-11 retry work: under a sustained Redis outage an in-flight chunk that used to abort on the first header-less 503/404 now sleeps and retries up to the BO's own DETECTION_ASYNC_MAX_WAIT_S, so its report row shifts from Incomplete (stale) to Incomplete (timeout) — same root cause, different-looking symptom; and a terminal write retrying up to TERMINAL_WRITE_BUDGET_S holds the single FIFO worker for that whole time, delaying every already-queued job behind it
nodes.norm_label: operational consequences of the 2026-08-11 retry work: under a sustained redis outage an in-flight chunk that used to abort on the first header-less 503/404 now sleeps and retries up to the bo's own detection_async_max_wait_s, so its report row shifts from incomplete (stale) to incomplete (timeout) — same root cause, different-looking symptom; and a terminal write retrying up to terminal_write_budget_s holds the single fifo worker for that whole time, delaying every already-queued job behind it

nodes.label: Post-verdict variant rescue (_variant_rescue, method suffixed +variant_rescue): re-probes the http/https and www/apex forms AFTER the decision matrix has run — the only point where verdict and requested URL coexist — with ONE scrape_html probe per variant instead of the retry cascade and validate_alternatives=False hardcoded; the first variant analysing to ok=True wins and analyzed_url carries the retained URL, observable in the BO report with zero BO-side change; never triggers when the caller supplied html_content
nodes.norm_label: post-verdict variant rescue (_variant_rescue, method suffixed +variant_rescue): re-probes the http/https and www/apex forms after the decision matrix has run — the only point where verdict and requested url coexist — with one scrape_html probe per variant instead of the retry cascade and validate_alternatives=false hardcoded; the first variant analysing to ok=true wins and analyzed_url carries the retained url, observable in the bo report with zero bo-side change; never triggers when the caller supplied html_content

nodes.label: Why the rescue sits after the verdict rather than in the Phase-2 gate: that gate only ever engages on a fetch that FAILS, so a fetch that SUCCEEDS but yields an unusable verdict (Check_nok_v2, fetch_empty_content) never reaches Phase 2 and stays locked to the URL form under test — exactly the case a variant repairs (groupe-denis.com redirecting to ibyd.fr only on http, rgb-solutions.green only on the apex)

nodes.label: Why every non-winning rescue outcome — no variant, a failed or timed-out probe, any exception during a variant's analysis, an invalid page, a challenge page, no French variant — leaves the original verdict unchanged and is deliberately never turned into a timeout: degrading a Check_nok_v2 into method='error' produces a verdict Pass 2 does not retry and that carries no cause, worse than the false negative the rescue exists to fix

nodes.label: _ITEM_WALL_CLOCK_S (300) is the single constant now backing all four batch wait_for() literals, but it is enforced ONLY on the batch paths: a single POST /detect calls _detect_single_url directly with no wait_for wrapping it, so on that path the 300s is purely an arithmetic input to the budget formula, not an actual enforced ceiling

nodes.label: Why a probe needs at least _MIN_PROBE_S (80s) of headroom before it starts: 45s worst-case BROWSER_LAUNCH_TIMEOUT_S launch + up to 30s domcontentloaded + the networkidle phase + slack, deliberately the worst case since preventing the worst case is the floor's whole purpose — below it a probe is likelier to be cancelled mid-navigation than to answer, the exact condition that orphans Playwright protocol callbacks (domain_fr.py:1451-1459)

nodes.label: VARIANT_RESCUE_BUDGET_S has three settings, not two: 0 is the intended silent kill-switch, 1 through _MIN_PROBE_S INCLUSIVE is an inert trap (the pre-flight check sees remaining < _MIN_PROBE_S and returns before a single probe runs), and only strictly > _MIN_PROBE_S is live — the boundary itself is dead on the Linux deployment target because remaining = deadline - time.monotonic() is always shaved slightly below the configured budget, while Windows' 15.625ms clock resolution makes it look live on a dev machine; main.py's lifespan logs a startup WARNING for 0 < budget <= _MIN_PROBE_S, never for 0

nodes.label: Job-level cost of the rescue: /detect-batch-async jobs are bounded by JOB_MAX_S (1500) and a job past it is marked failed(job_timeout) returning NO results at all — every item in the batch discarded, not just the slow one — while the rescue adds up to VARIANT_RESCUE_BUDGET_S of wall clock per RESCUED item; after enabling it, watch detection_variant_rescue_total against detect_async_jobs_terminal_total{status=failed} carrying error=job_timeout, since losing a whole batch to buy back a handful of false negatives is strictly worse than the defect being fixed

nodes.label: Why the lexical signal ships inert: the motivating false negative (automatismes.net — clean French prose, no html lang, no hreflang, no distinctive TLD, fastText confidently wrong) never reaches Case 8, because that case's soft_from_fasttext guard requires fastText itself to have said fr, which it did not; widening the guard needs a threshold and the only evidence so far is six short samples, so LEXICAL_OBSERVATION_MIN_DISTINCT=3 is an OBSERVATION threshold, deliberately permissive to surface borderline cases, distinct from the activation threshold under consideration (5), which is NOT implemented
